title: WHEN THE PRIESTS' FEET TOUCH THE WATER

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now then, choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe. And as soon as the priests who carry the ark of the Lord — the Lord of all the earth — set foot in the Jordan, its waters flowing downstream will be cut off and stand up in a heap." — Josh 3:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the plan, spoken before it happens. The waters would not part while the priests stood safely on the bank deliberating. They would part only when the priests' feet actually stepped into the river. God required a step of faith first, and then He would work the miracle.

This is one of Scripture's clearest pictures of how faith and God's power meet. God does not usually part the waters and then invite us to walk. He calls us to walk toward the waters, trusting Him, and He parts them as we go. The miracle followed the obedience; it did not precede it.

That takes courage, because stepping into a flooded river looks like folly to human eyes. But faith is willing to look foolish in order to trust God. The priests had God's promise, and a promise from the Lord of all the earth is more solid than the ground beneath our feet.

Notice too the twelve men, one from each tribe. God was including the whole nation, preparing them to remember and mark this moment together. God's works are meant to be shared and remembered by His whole people.

Jesus called us to a faith that steps out, like Peter walking on the water at His word (Matt 14:29). We may not always feel ready, but God's promise is sure. Take the step, and watch what God does.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where is God asking you to "step into the water" before you see it part?
2. Are you willing to look foolish in order to trust God's promise?
3. What promise of God can you stand on more firmly than the ground itself?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord of all the earth, give me faith to step into the water at Your word. I trust Your promise more than what my eyes can see. Amen.
